title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government confirms it will adopt the Committee’s 2020 recommendations on AI reliability and transparency, setting up new regulatory standards and oversight mechanisms to ensure safer, fairer systems. It also announces funding for research, public consultation, and initiatives that promote accountability and ethical use of AI.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its plan to oversee how artificial intelligence is used in UK qualifications, aiming to keep exams fair and reliable. The policy responds to requests from the education, science, and business ministers to ensure AI tools are regulated properly within the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted materials are used to train and develop AI systems, analyzing the legal and ethical implications. It assesses the impact of copyright laws on AI innovation and suggests guidelines for balancing creators' rights with technological advancement.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government replies to the Lords Select Committee’s AI report by reaffirming its commitment to responsible AI development and outlining concrete steps such as strengthening regulation, investing in research, and encouraging international cooperation. It stresses the need to balance innovation with public safety and privacy to keep the UK competitive in the global AI market.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: It defines the purpose and scope of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards. It also answers common questions and explains the committee’s structure, tasks and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee as part of its inquiry into AI governance, outlining the organisation’s views on how artificial intelligence should be regulated. The submission likely addresses issues such as safety, transparency, accountability, and the need for clear policy frameworks to manage AI risks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how artificial intelligence will shape the regulation of medical products, aiming to align emerging technologies with current safety and efficacy standards. It outlines steps to incorporate the principles of the AI White Paper—such as transparency, accountability, and risk mitigation—into regulatory frameworks to protect patients while fostering innovation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential in AI for its size, strengthening national security. It focuses on building robust AI capabilities, fostering collaboration, and upholding ethical standards to position the defence force as a global leader in AI technology.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan shows how the Department for Transport will team up with the transport industry to use AI to improve services and safety. It also lays out measures to identify and control the risks that could come with new AI technologies.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyrighted material is being used to train and improve artificial intelligence systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines progress, challenges, and recommendations for balancing the needs of AI developers with the rights of copyright holders.
